$comment: Single source of truth for the MikePDF IPC protocol (ADR-0005). tools/MikePDF.ProtocolGen turns this into the C# and C++ codecs.
Wire format. A frame is a 4-byte little-endian body length followed by a MessagePack body of at most maxFrameBytes.
Request body:  [requestId:u64, documentId:u32, deadlineMs:u32, messageType:u16, payload:array]
Response body: [requestId:u64, status:u16, messageType:u16, payload:array|nil]  (payload is an array exactly when the status carries one)
A payload is a MessagePack array of exactly the declared fields, in key order. The key IS the array index, so keys are contiguous from 0.

Stability: a message id, a field key, a field type and an enum value are never reused or changed within a schemaVersion. Any layout change bumps schemaVersion; Hello and HelloReply keep their layout in every version so that the version check itself can always be decoded. On a mismatch the peer is killed, not accommodated.
Messages have no nesting: variable-size collections are parallel arrays tied together with sameLengthAs.
Every variable-size field has a limit and the generator rejects a schema in which any legal message cannot fit in one frame.

enums.name: Status
enums.$comment: Response status. Values with payload=true carry a reply payload, all others carry nil. Codes are master prompt 6.4. ProtocolError is also what a decoder reports for a malformed frame and InvalidArgument for a well-formed frame that breaks a schema limit.

values.name: ShellHandler
values.$comment: The native thumbnail provider or preview handler DLL in Explorer's process (docs/features/shell-extensions.md). It is only ever a client: it sends Hello to ShellHost (ADR-0018), which accepts no other kind, and no peer sends it a request. An engine refuses a Hello of this kind: the handler must never reach one.

fields.name: processKind
fields.doc: Kind of the sending process.

fields.name: pdfiumVersion
fields.doc: Empty for hosts without PDFium.

messages.name: Ping
messages.$comment: Pong carries the peer's progress counter (schema 5). It is answered by the I/O thread, so it keeps coming while the thread that does the work is busy or stuck; what moves is the counter, which that thread bumps whenever it makes progress. The broker kills an engine on a missed pong (the I/O thread is gone) or on a request that is overdue while the counter has stood still for the stall timeout (the work thread is stuck), never on a request that is merely slow while the counter moves. See docs/adr/0004 amendment A3.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: Units of work the peer's work thread has done so far: it counts up, wraps at 2^64, and is compared for change only. 0 and a constant mean nothing happened; hosts that do all their work on the I/O thread report 0.

messages.name: AttachSlotRing
messages.$comment: Sent once, right after Hello, to an engine. The section handle is duplicated into the engine by the broker (no handle is ever inherited), so its value arrives here, not on the command line. RenderTile is refused until the ring is attached. slotCount and slotSize mirror SlotRing: at most 1024 slots (the slotIndex limit) of a multiple of 4096 bytes up to 64 MiB; the engine also checks that the section is at least slotCount x slotSize and that the total is at most 1 GiB.

fields.name: handle
fields.doc: Value of the section handle duplicated into the engine, with write access.

fields.name: slotSize
fields.doc: Bytes per slot.

fields.name: handle
fields.doc: Value of the file handle duplicated into the engine.

fields.name: pdfVersion
fields.doc: Version times ten, as PDFium reports it (17 = PDF 1.7). 0 = unknown.

fields.name: permissions
fields.doc: PDF permission bits, as in the /P entry.

messages.name: GetPageSizes
messages.$comment: count is capped at 5000 so that a full reply (5000 x (5+5+1) bytes) fits one 64 KiB frame; callers page through larger documents.

fields.name: widths
fields.doc: Points.

fields.name: rotations
fields.doc: Quarter turns clockwise.

messages.name: GetOutline
messages.$comment: One level of the bookmark tree, a window of siblings at a time, so a tree is expanded lazily and a reply always fits a frame. path names the parent by the sibling index taken at each level from the root (empty = the top level); it is addressing by position, not by a handle, so it survives an engine restart. total is the number of siblings at that level (the engine stops counting at 100000). Destinations are in PDF user space of the destination page; convert with GetPageBoxes.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: Sibling index at each level, root first. At most 16 levels.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: Destination kind: 0 none, 1 page, 2 page and y, 3 page, x and y, 4 external address, 5 any other action.

fields.name: pages
fields.doc: Zero-based destination page; 0 unless kind is 1, 2 or 3.

messages.name: GetPageLinks
messages.$comment: The link annotations of one page, a window at a time. Rectangles and destinations are in PDF user space (convert with GetPageBoxes). The address of an external link is not sent here; the caller asks for it with GetLinkUri when the link is activated.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Links on the page; the engine stops counting at 100000.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: As GetOutlineReply.kinds.

messages.name: GetLinkUri
messages.$comment: The address behind an external link (kind 4 from GetPageLinks). Unsupported when the address is longer than 2048 bytes, is not valid UTF-8 or holds control characters; InvalidArgument when the link is not an external one.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: Position of the link in the order GetPageLinks reports.

messages.name: GetPageBoxes
messages.$comment: What the caller needs to convert PDF user space to page space (MikePDF.Core PageGeometry): the MediaBox, the CropBox when the page has one, and /Rotate in quarter turns.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: The page's own /Rotate in quarter turns clockwise.

messages.name: GetPageText
messages.$comment: The characters of one page in PDFium's order, a window at a time (a dense page is several replies; 2048 characters x 24 bytes fit a frame). One entry per UTF-16 code unit, with its loose box in PDF user space. The engine stops at 200000 characters and says so in truncated.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Characters on the page (at most 200000).

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: The page has more characters than the engine reports.

fields.name: units
fields.doc: UTF-16 code units.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0: PDFium made this character up (a space or line break). Bit 1: a hyphen at the end of a line.

messages.name: SearchPage
messages.$comment: Finds a phrase in one page. starts and lengths are in the character numbering of GetPageText. The engine reports at most 2048 matches per page and says so in truncated.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 match case, bit 1 whole words only.

messages.name: GetDocumentDetails
messages.$comment: What the properties dialog needs beyond GetDocumentInfo (schema 4). The two dates are the file's own text, e.g. D:20240115103000+10'00' (the broker parses them and shows what it cannot parse as text). securityRevision is the standard security handler's /R: 0 when the document is not encrypted. userPermissions is the /P the file gives an ordinary user, whoever opened the file, while GetDocumentInfoReply.permissions is what applies to this session (everything, after the owner password). formType is PDFium's: 0 none, 1 AcroForm, 2 XFA, 3 XFA foreground. Fonts are those the text on the first pages is drawn with, found by walking the page objects within a time and page budget; fontNames are printable ASCII (base font names, possibly with a subset prefix such as ABCDEF+), fontFlags bit 0 is 'embedded'. fontsComplete says every page was walked; otherwise fontPagesScanned says how many were.

fields.name: fontFlags
fields.doc: Bit 0: the font program is embedded in the file.

messages.name: GetViewerPreferences
messages.$comment: The /ViewerPreferences the reader and the print dialog use (schema 5). docs/features/print.md calls it id 26, which GetDocumentDetails took in schema 4. Every value is a clamped, bounded reading of what the file says, never the raw entry: a hostile or ill-typed entry reads as absent. direction: the reading direction (/Direction), 0 left to right, 1 right to left, 2 absent. printScaling: 0 absent, 1 none (/PrintScaling /None), 2 the application default (/AppDefault). numCopies: /NumCopies from 1 to 99, 0 when absent or outside that. duplex: 0 absent, 1 simplex, 2 flip short edge, 3 flip long edge. The print page ranges are zero-based inclusive pairs (/PrintPageRange is 1-based in the file) in file order, at most 64, each first <= last and inside the document.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 annotations, bit 1 form fields.

messages.name: RenderBand
messages.$comment: A horizontal band of a page for printing (ADR-0011, docs/features/print.md 11). RenderTile stays limited to 1024 px for the viewing path; a band is as wide as the page at the printer's resolution, so it has its own limits, its own semantic checks and its own fuzz target. The page is laid out at pageWidthPx x pageHeightPx device pixels (the broker computed them from dpi, the page size and the rotation) and the band is the rows bandTop to bandTop + bandHeight of that, drawn into the slot as BGRA over white with stride 4 x pageWidthPx. The engine and the broker both check that pageWidthPx x bandHeight x 4 fits the slot and that the band lies inside the page. flags: bit 0 annotations, bit 1 form fields, bit 2 printing mode (PDFium's FPDF_PRINTING: no screen-only annotations, no LCD text). The reserved bit 3 is not allowed: max 7.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 annotations, bit 1 form fields, bit 2 printing mode.

messages.name: ValidateStructure
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only. 256 issues of at most 192 message bytes fit one frame (512-byte messages would not).

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: More issues were found than fit.

messages.name: AppendAnnotations
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only (schema 6, save-pipeline 3.3 stage 4). Appends one incremental update for the annotation edits in the edit blob (save-pipeline 11.3: a second format, MessagePack, read from editsHandle; not a frame) to the base document and writes base plus update to outputHandle. Every file is a handle duplicated into the host: baseHandle and editsHandle are read-only, outputHandle has write access and is empty. pageCount is the base's page count the edits were made against; a different count is InvalidArgument. A status other than Ok carries no payload, so a refusal the broker needs the reason for is an Ok reply with ok false and issueCodes (PdfErrorCode) and issueMessages in the shape of ValidateStructureReply: the strict parser refuses the base, the base is encrypted or over a limit, the page count differs, an edit's expectation does not hold. InvalidArgument: a handle that is not a file, an edits length that is not the file's, a blob that does not decode. Timeout and PermissionDenied as for ValidateStructure.

fields.name: editsLength
fields.doc: The blob's length in bytes, at most 256 MiB.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: More issues were found than fit.

messages.name: RewriteDocument
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only (schema 6, save-pipeline 3.3): a full rewrite of the base into outputHandle, for Save As 'Rewrite the whole file' and for a flattened copy. flags: bit 0 draw form fields into the pages and remove them, bit 1 draw comments and markup into the pages and remove them (max 3). The output holds only what the catalog can reach: no older revision, no flattened annotation. Handles as for AppendAnnotations. The reply says what was done; ok is false with issues as for AppendAnnotations, and the statuses are as there.

messages.name: VerifyAnnotations
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only (schema 6, save-pipeline 3.3 stage 5): a second, independent strict parse of the base and of a finished output. It checks that the output has pageCount pages and that, for each page named in pages, the number of annotations that are not links, popups or widgets is the base's number plus added minus removed, where added and removed are the broker's model (what the edits say). mismatches lists the pages (from pages) whose count differs. The broker sends at most 2048 pages per call and calls again for more. Both handles are read-only and valid in the host.

fields.name: ok
fields.doc: Both files parse strictly and the output has pageCount pages.

messages.name: ShellOpen
messages.$comment: MikePDF.ShellHost only (schema 5, ADR-0018, spike S6b section 'Protocol: messages and schema v5'): the first message a thumbnail provider or preview handler DLL (ProcessKind ShellHandler) sends on its pipe after Hello. The connection is the session. Handle direction: section is a handle value valid in the SENDING process (the handler), with read access; ShellHost duplicates it from the process at the other end of the pipe (GetNamedPipeClientProcessId, then DuplicateHandle), which a handler running at Low integrity can still allow. bytes is the file size (the section may be larger). There is no password: a shell never prompts. The reply's documentId is the session, and every later message of the session carries it in the envelope.

fields.name: section
fields.doc: A section handle valid in the handler (the sender), read access.

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: The file size, at most 32 MiB.

fields.name: documentId
fields.doc: The session: the envelope documentId of ShellRenderPage and ShellClose.

fields.name: firstWidth
fields.doc: Points.

fields.name: firstHeight
fields.doc: Points.

messages.name: ShellRenderPage
messages.$comment: Renders one page to fit maxWidth x maxHeight (16 to 1024: the tile limit, to be raised when a band message serves the shell) into a section the handler made. pixels is a section handle valid in the SENDING process (the handler) with write access, duplicated by ShellHost the same way as ShellOpen.section; pixelBytes is at least maxWidth x maxHeight x 4 (the handler's check, repeated by ShellHost against the section). flags: bit 0 draw annotations, nothing else (max 1). The pixels are in the caller's section. The reply values the schema cannot tie to the request, and which the handler must check before it builds a bitmap: width <= maxWidth, height <= maxHeight, stride == 4 x width.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 annotations.

fields.name: pixels
fields.doc: A section handle valid in the handler (the sender), write access.

fields.name: stride
fields.doc: Equal to 4 x width.

messages.name: ShellClose
messages.$comment: Optional: closing the pipe ends the session just the same.
